software: LumiTouch reply system. Fiber-optic response device for collection of behavioral data in magnetoencephalography and functional magnetic resonance imaging experiments. In collaboration with John Kidder, CEO, and Doug Broadfoot, Lightwave Medical Inc. Vancouver, B.C., Canada. Spin off company now makes and services the device https://natatech.com/products/complete-response-systems.
Conversion programs for creating ANALYZE format images from GE structural and functional data sets. In collaboration with Scott Morrison.

MRI off-line reconstruction software for EPI data on the Silicon Graphics Workstations. In collaboration with Bryan Mock, University of Wisconsin – Madison; General Electric Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI.

CIRC – computer program designed to monitor and analyze behavioral performance online during behavioral, event-related potential, magnetoencephalography, and functional magnetic resonance imaging experiments. In collaboration with Arthur Jones and Clif Kussmaul
Digitize – Solaris based high-resolution EEG acquisition system. Designed for collection of up to 128 channels of EEG for brain mapping and source localization. In collaboration with Arthur Jones.

Talairach atlas labeling system. Software designed to automatically search the results of functional imaging data and label with brain structures from the Talairach atlas. In collaboration with Adrien Desjardins and Peter Liddle.

Visual and Auditory Presentation Package (VAPP). Software designed for presenting visual and auditory stimuli for behavioral, event-related potential, magnetoencephalography, and functional magnetic resonance imaging experiments. In collaboration with Tony Gray, Peter Liddle, Ron Mangun, Steve Hillyard, Steve Luck and Marty Woldorff

Group Independent Component Analyses Software (GIFT and EEGIFT). Software designed to permit end-users to use Independent Component Analyses to analyses multimodal neuroimaging data. Effort directed by Dr. Vince Calhoun.

CIRC 2.0 – a collaboration with Claude. Code Integration and Response Computer (CIRC) is a program designed to monitor and analyze behavioral performance during behavioral, event-related potential, magnetoencephalography, and functional magnetic resonance imaging experiments. CIRC also integrates MRI scanner codes (every TR during fMRI) to permit perfect synchronicity between the MRI scanner, stimulus presentation (E-Prime, Presentation, Cogent, etc), and response devices. Real-time display highlight’s individual reaction times, hits, misses, and other behavioral data. CIRC log files are parsed to generate vectors for fMRI or other analyses. Being reprogrammed in python to enable more widespread use. In development, soon to be added to Kiehl lab GITHUB.
presentations_summary: More than 400 scientific presentations from 1993 to 2026, including 196 invited lectures and keynote or plenary addresses.

history.title: Undergraduate training at UC Davis
history.text: Kiehl completed his undergraduate thesis with Michael (Rick) Levenson. Their collaboration produced the Levenson Self-Report Psychopathy Scale (LSRP), now widely used to assess psychopathic traits outside forensic settings. At the UC Davis Center for Neuroscience he worked as a research assistant with Michael Gazzaniga and George (Ron) Mangun, training in experimental design and brain-imaging analysis.

history.title: Graduate work at the University of British Columbia
history.text: He earned his doctorate in psychology and neuroscience in 2000, co-mentored by Robert Hare, author of the Psychopathy Checklist-Revised (PCL-R), and Peter Liddle, a co-founder of the Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) software. He published more than 20 peer-reviewed papers as a graduate student, including the first fMRI study of brain dysfunction in criminal psychopaths, and is a certified trainer for clinical use of the PCL-R.

history.title: Yale and the Institute of Living
history.text: In 2001 he joined the Yale University faculty in Psychiatry and Psychology and directed the Clinical Cognitive Neuroscience Laboratory at the Olin Neuropsychiatry Research Center (Institute of Living, Hartford Hospital), working on psychopathy and schizophrenia.

history.title: The Mind Research Network and the University of New Mexico
history.text: In 2007 he was jointly recruited by the Mind Research Network and the University of New Mexico, where he is Professor of Psychology with secondary appointments in Neurosciences and Law. He has been Executive Science Officer of the Mind Research Network since 2011.

history.title: The Mind Mobile MRI System
history.text: No prison in the United States has an MRI scanner, so Kiehl designed and built a one-of-a-kind mobile MRI system, delivered in 2007, that brings the scanner to the people being studied. It has since scanned more than 6,000 incarcerated people across a dozen states, creating the largest forensic neuroimaging repository in the world. A second, twin mobile MRI was delivered in September 2019.

history.title: Neuroscience and the law
history.text: He was an original member of the MacArthur Foundation Law and Neuroscience Project led by Michael Gazzaniga, chaired its Psychopathy Working Group, and co-edited the Handbook on Psychopathy and Law (Oxford) with Walter Sinnott-Armstrong. He lectures to judges, lawyers, probation and corrections officials and the public, and worked with the Federal Judicial Center on a neuroscience curriculum for federal judges.
